nodes.label: PostHog ingestion worker slice
nodes.intent: A bounded source-preserving adoption of admission, processing, result routing and acknowledgment. Not the full ingestion fleet or an end-to-end delivery proof.
nodes.why: Use existing source seams and original oracles to distinguish canonical graph omissions from canvas problems. Root aliases remain unchanged; missing connections must stay visible as an adoption finding.

nodes.label: Output destinations
nodes.intent: Provides named destinations to the result router. Dead-letter and redirected records become producer effects; ordinary successful events continue on the processing path.
nodes.prose:
## known limits
- Fake-producer tests do not establish Kafka durability, delivery uniqueness or the completeness of configured destinations.
nodes.why: This spec covers the copied files in this directory, not every upstream module under the same directory. Named test evidence is scoped to its selected fixtures. Imports and declared reliance do not establish end-to-end satisfaction.

nodes.label: Deferred effect scheduler

definition.title: Acknowledgment barrier
definition.promise: Successful acknowledgment follows the named completion barrier rather than mere receipt or submission.
definition.appliesWhen: A producer relies on an acknowledgment to retire responsibility for submitted work.
definition.excludes: Durability, query visibility and downstream exactly-once behavior not promised by that barrier.
definition.falsifier: Hold settlement unresolved and observe successful acknowledgment or retirement of its in-flight responsibility.
definition.demoteWhen: The binding uses completed without specifying which event retires which responsibility.

distinctFrom.because: This delays reporting success; commit ordering delays issuing an external effect.

definition.title: Graceful drain
definition.promise: Shutdown stops the declared admission path and gives already-accepted work its promised settlement/drain opportunity before closing, with an explicit deadline outcome.
definition.appliesWhen: A service closes while work is in flight.
definition.excludes: Unbounded waiting, guaranteed completion of stalled dependencies and work outside the captured drain population.
definition.falsifier: Initiate stop with a settling accepted batch and observe its stream closed before its acknowledgment within the allowed drain budget.
definition.demoteWhen: The definition cannot state which work was accepted before shutdown or treats forced timeout as successful completion.

distinctFrom.because: A per-work acknowledgment rule does not ensure shutdown keeps its transport alive long enough to deliver it.

definition.title: Cancellation releases capacity
definition.promise: Canceled waiting work loses its queue claim and any subsequently granted capacity is returned rather than consumed by dead work.
definition.appliesWhen: Cancelable work waits for a scarce slot.
definition.excludes: Stopping already-running server computation and removing already-issued irreversible effects.
definition.falsifier: Cancel a queued waiter, release one slot, and observe the dead waiter consume it while a live waiter remains blocked.
definition.demoteWhen: The supposed cancellation property only hides presentation and has no queue or resource claim to release.

distinctFrom.because: A FIFO queue can be fair among live entries yet leak every canceled entry's capacity.

definition.title: Fair admission
definition.promise: When capacity becomes available, eligible contenders receive service according to the declared scheduling order rather than accidental races.
definition.appliesWhen: Multiple eligible contenders share a scheduling resource with an explicit fairness policy.
definition.excludes: Wall-clock latency bounds, equal throughput and progress while no slots become available.
definition.falsifier: Queue A before B under FIFO policy, free a slot, and grant it to B while A remains eligible.
definition.demoteWhen: Fairness cannot be expressed as a concrete service-order relation with explicit progress assumptions.

distinctFrom.because: A capacity-safe scheduler can indefinitely favor the same contender.

definition.title: Bounded admission
definition.promise: The named admission boundary does not admit more simultaneously active work than its configured capacity.
definition.appliesWhen: A scheduler or service imposes a concurrency ceiling.
definition.excludes: Bounds on every buffer, memory allocation, per-tenant fairness and time-window rate limits.
definition.falsifier: Keep the configured number of streams active and successfully admit an additional stream instead of applying overflow policy.
definition.demoteWhen: No observable counted active unit exists, or the candidate conflates instantaneous concurrency with cumulative rate.

distinctFrom.because: Concurrency counts active work; a rate budget counts consumption over time even after work finishes.
